newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: COLOMBIA PESO SLIDES AMID GUERRILLA WAR FEARS.
newsitem.headline: COLOMBIA PESO SLIDES AMID GUERRILLA WAR FEARS.

text.p: Colombia's peso dived 11.45 pesos to close at a historic low of 1,131.8 as investors scrambled for greenbacks amid new fears that the government was losing ground to the country's leftist guerrillas, interbank traders said.

The sharp peso slide was sparked by calls from ruling Liberal Party lawmakers for President Ernesto Samper to assume emergency powers to combat Marxist rebels, who have launched a wave of attacks to disrupt forthcoming local elections in October.
Other legislators called for Samper to stand down and face impeachment. In a congressional debate late Tuesday, the Congressmen said he had lost control of the country.

Currency dealers said dollar demand was fueled by foreign banks and those with close ties to foreign institutions preparing to send cash out of the country in the event of an upturn in Colombia's three-decade-old guerrilla war.

"The dollar was driven up by banks looking to build up positions. There was a limited influx of greenbacks into the market and neither the oil nor the coffee sector took advantage of the soaring dollar rate to pump export earnings into the market," one dealer said.
Dealers said the peso slide could continue Thursday in the face of sparse dollar offer and high peso liquidity.
The peso opened at the intraday high of 1,120.8 and sank to an intraday low of 1,132.7. Dealers reported 514 trades worth $256 million, above the daily average of about $180 million.
